text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000599 bills 99215 at well above expected rates across every complexity tier, including many low-complexity patients, but the few documented 99215 claims all support the billed level, so the evidence does not settle the question.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The claims pattern leans toward upcoding. The provider's 99215 share runs roughly three times the all-provider share in every complexity stratum, including patients with zero conditions. About a third of 99215s fall on patients with 0 or 1 conditions, with diagnoses such as low back pain (M54.50), UTI (N39.0), URI (J06.9) and follow-up (Z09), for example C0313065, C0314665 and C0313449. Against that, the records review is too thin to judge: only 3 documented 99215 claims, all supported at high MDM, and no data-reviewed notes that lacked a lab or test line. Two of those supported notes, C0313960 (back pain, no chronic conditions) and C0313741, are on low-complexity patients, so a reviewer should first pull those charts to check whether the high-MDM documentation reflects a real encounter or a templated or inflated note. The next priority is a larger targeted records request for low-complexity 99215 claims from the sample list."}
